_comment: The second famous place (2026-09-04, section 60I), and the darkest scene in the menu now that the car park has gone. It was written as a lantern-lit back street; the owner asked for the city as everybody knows it, and the card (assets/places/tokyo-night.jpg) is a wide crossing at night under lit signboards, empty, with a vending machine, a phone box and a bicycle on the corner. This preset describes that card. The rule every famous place follows here survives one layer down: the tape prompt forbids readable characters and brand logos, so the signboards are lit panels on the tape rather than words.
label: Tokyo, at night
_passersby_comment: a wide crossing at night is a thoroughfare; the card is empty because a generated crowd invents faces, but the tape wants the street alive behind the subject. Strangers stay away from the lens; the composer writes that clause, not this file.

prompt._comment: Two light sources that do not match -- the cold white of the signboards from above and the warm shopfronts at ground level -- is the same trick the kitchen preset plays with a bulb and a window, and it is what makes a night street read as real rather than lit for a shoot. The wet asphalt is doing the work a second light would: every sign appears twice.
prompt.scene: a wide crossing in Tokyo at night, the buildings around it faced with lit signboards and one big glowing screen, white crosswalk stripes across wet asphalt, a lit drinks vending machine and a phone box on the corner, a bicycle with a front basket leaning on a pole, a tangle of overhead lines above the traffic light
prompt.light: the signboards and the screen are the main source, cold white with red and pink spilling down the fronts, warm light from the shopfronts at ground level, the sky above gone to black
prompt.lens: wide from the kerb across the crossing, the far corner going soft behind the signs, every light drawing a hard point, a little barrel bend at the edges
prompt.framing: chest-up on the kerb beside the vending machine, the crossing and the lit corner behind
prompt._moment: What is HAPPENING, not what is in frame. A brief with no action in it is a portrait brief, and the model answers it with a portrait -- squared to the camera, arms hanging, waiting. Somebody caught halfway through something ordinary is what a real snapshot looks like.
prompt.moment: waiting at the light with one hand resting on the bicycle's handlebar
prompt.eraProps: a flip phone with a dangling charm, a lit drinks vending machine, a phone box with a folding door, a clear plastic umbrella hooked on a bicycle handlebar, a folded paper map

motionHint: the signboards flicker on and off in turn, a taxi crosses the far side of the crossing, and the wet asphalt holds and loses each light as it moves
_scripts: Three fifteen-second scripts, one picked per order by the scripted arc (compose/prompt.mjs). Each is three shots at five seconds, written around the objects already in this place, so what happens comes from where it is. Every shot names the person, the first has them turned toward the lens, the last keeps their whole head in frame and ends on them, and none names anybody holding the camera. Tests in compose-prompt.test.js hold every one of those.

scripts.name: The light changes
shots: Medium. They are waiting at the crossing, turned toward the lens, then stepping out onto the white stripes as the lights change, camera moving backwards ahead of them.
Wide. They cross the wet asphalt with strangers further back, looking up at the big glowing screen, camera moving backwards ahead of them.
Medium close. Reaching the far kerb, they turn to the lens and laugh, their whole head in frame, camera settling on them.

scripts.name: The vending machine
shots: Medium. They are pressing a button on the lit drinks vending machine, turned toward the lens as the can drops, camera holding on them.
Medium. They crack the can open and drink, the signboards flickering on and off in the background, camera easing round to stay in front of them.
Medium close. They raise the can to the lens, their whole head in frame, camera settling on them.

scripts.name: The bicycle
shots: Medium. They are unhooking the clear plastic umbrella from the bicycle leaning on the pole, turned toward the lens, camera holding on them.
Wide. They wheel the bicycle out and ride a slow loop across the crossing, the lights sliding over the wet asphalt, camera turning with them.
Medium close. They stop beside the lens and ring the bell at it, their whole head in frame, camera settling on them.

lookOverride._comment: Lit signboards are cooler than paper lanterns, so the warm push is smaller than the first draft of this preset carried, and halation is open nearly as far as Times Square: every sign and the vending machine's front are blown highlights on wet ground. The most grain in the menu, because the scene is dark without being flat.

ambience._comment: A city at night heard from a kerb: the hum of the vending machine and distant traffic as one low bed, a slow shallow swell for the taxi the motionHint sends across, and a short echo because the fronts around a crossing are close. Quieter than the car park was -- the crossing in the card is empty, and the point of the picture is that nothing much is happening under all that light.
